name: Stipple engraving
summary: A way to make tone in an intaglio plate with dots of many sizes. The prints look like chalk drawings.
how: Mark the plate with dots, made with an etching needle, a burin or a roulette tool.
Make dots close and large for the dark areas, and small and wide apart for the light.
Print in red chalk colour (sanguine) to copy a chalk drawing.
Use no hatching in the soft areas, so that the face has a smooth tone.

origin.note: Giulio Campagnola made tone with dots of the burin in place of lines.

adoptions.via: Francesco Bartolozzi and William Wynne Ryland make stipple engravings in red and black for the London market.
Francesco Bartolozzi engraves portraits in stipple, and some in colour, for the London market.
